h1: When is an on-site drywell or stormwater infiltration system required in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Drywell and Infiltration Rules: Stormwater Planning
description: Learn when Newton stormwater review may apply and which drywell design and sizing details need confirmation.
short_answer: Newton's stormwater ordinance regulates certain land-disturbance and new-impervious-area projects, but the sources reviewed do not establish one universal drywell size or a citywide rule requiring every homeowner to install a drywell. Whether an infiltration system is needed depends on the project, site conditions, and Newton's stormwater requirements.

facts.text: Newton's stormwater ordinance identifies land disturbance over 5,000 square feet and certain residential projects creating 401 to 1,000 square feet of new impervious area as permit categories.
Newton Engineering reviews site plans involving new drainage and expansions of impervious area.

qa.q: Is a drywell always required for a new roof or driveway?
qa.a: The official sources reviewed do not establish that universal rule. Ask Engineering whether the project requires infiltration, a stormwater plan, or another approved drainage approach.
